messages:
jordan: Heads-up — large enterprise customer (acme-health) is getting intermittent 429s starting ~08:10 UTC, but their dashboard shows quota remaining. They reported repeated retries and a pile of duplicate requests hitting our backend. Raising to eng-sre.

maya: thanks, tagging @sanjay and @aj. any quick triage data? customer shared request id 0a1b2c and a sample response header: `x-rate-limit: 100/60`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 1690004970`.

aj: looking at logs for tenant acme-health. I see a burst-window refill task failing with repeated `cache.get` timeouts to redis around 08:09–08:12. Several workers retried and then enqueued requests — looks like token state got out of sync.

sanjay: i see the same. quota service emitted `refill_error` and then a fallback that allowed queued requests to replay once redis recovered — that replay seems to have double-counted tokens for some tenants and left others with negative remaining (appearing as 0).

jordan: customer says their app did 200 retries in a loop and then hit throttles, causing degraded UX. They want scope of impact and ETA for fix.

maya: immediate mitigation: can we temporarily exclude acme-health from burst accounting so they get baseline throughput while we fix state?

aj: yes, I can add a tenant-level emergency bypass rule for 1 hour. running:
```
# emergency bypass
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://controlplane.internal/tenants/acme-health/bypass -d '{"reason":"support escal","expires_in":3600}'
```

sanjay: note that bypass will let them through but won't repair the leaked token state. we need a reconciliation job.

ops-bot: deploy?id=deploy-3812 starting rollback of `quota-refactor` to v2.12 — initiated by aj at 08:26 UTC :hammer_and_wrench:

aj: rolling back the recent quota refactor that touched refill scheduling. rollback in progress, monitoring redis connections.

maya: thanks. @jordan please tell the customer: 1) emergency bypass created, 2) we identified a regression in quota refill scheduling causing token miscounts, 3) rollback underway, 4) we'll run a reconciliation job and follow up with full postmortem.

jordan: relayed to customer, they asked for ETA on reconciliation and whether any billing implications.

aj: reconciliation plan: 1) stop refill workers (done via rollback), 2) run a one-off script to recalc bucket levels from request histories: `python tools/reconcile_buckets.py --tenant acme-health --since 2026-03-16T00:00Z`, 3) apply corrected counts, 4) re-enable workers behind feature flag. estimate 45–90 minutes.

sanjay: billing impact: if requests were double-counted or dropped we should flag for manual billing review. I'll open a billing-ticket and mark affected windows.

maya: operational items for post-incident: - add circuit-breaker on refill task to avoid cascading retries - add metric `refill_error_rate` alert threshold - add end-to-end test simulating redis timeouts - add tenant-level audit endpoints for current token state.

aj: reconcile job started at 08:40 UTC. verbose output snippet: `reconcile: scanned 1.2M events, corrected 1 tenant, applied delta -3420 tokens`.

jordan: customer confirmed throughput restored after bypass and reconciliation. they appreciate the quick patch but want a write-up.

maya: assigning owners: aj -> rollback + reconcile ops and follow-up PR; sanjay -> billing review + alerting; jordan -> customer comms & summary; i'll own the postmortem doc.

sanjay: created billing ticket #BILL-5623 and alert ticket #OBS-8301.

aj: PR opened to add circuit-breaker + metrics: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quota-service/pull/786

maya: final notes: incident window 08:09–08:48 UTC. root cause: mis-scheduled refill tasks after `quota-refactor` leading to cache timeouts and replayed queued requests. impact: small number of tenants saw duplicated replays and transient 429s. follow-ups scheduled this week. :white_check_mark:
